ActLevel.description: How far a grant may act on panes (docs/grants.md). Each level includes the ones before it.

observed.description: What was observed in tmux afterwards, for example the new pane id.

reason.description: Why it failed or why the outcome is unknown.

by.description: Who answered: owner:N, an app instance, or `dreamer` when the session closed first.

AgentApprovalRequest.description: The harness asks the user before going on. Answer with agent.sessions.approve or agent.sessions.deny.

expires_unix_ms.description: The harness answers by itself after this.

options.description: Choices offered; empty for a yes or no question.

AgentEvent.description: One provider hook report, as dream hook sends it.

detail.description: The notification type, or why a session ended.

event.description: The provider's event name, such as SessionStart or Notification.

hook_pid.description: The reporting hook process; its ancestry finds the run. It is never the run itself.

AgentRun.description: One agent run, by evidence. State says only what is known: never inferred from titles, CPU, or output.

helpers.description: Processes serving it (tools, servers), not counted as runs.

instrumentation.description: passive (found from its process only) or hooks (its provider's hooks report to the daemon).

session_id.description: The provider's session, when its hooks report it.

started_unix_ms.description: With host and pid, the run's identity.

state.description: passive: running. hooks: active, working, waiting_for_permission, idle (a turn ended), ended, or stale (no report for a while).

notes.description: Hosts that could not be asked, and why.

hosts.description: Connected hosts to ask too; `*` means every live host.

detail.description: Why it is detached, or what went wrong at start.

grant.description: The session's grant: the outer limit for everything its harness does through Dreamer.

harness_session.description: The harness's own session id, kept for resume.

pid.description: The harness process while it runs.

for_pane.description: Answer for the app in this app pane, as a desktop drawing its `transcript`'s approval card: the app's grant must allow this method and the session must be one the app may see, as well as the caller's.

option.description: For a request with options, the one chosen when approving.

cwd.description: The harness's working directory; default the daemon's home directory.

grant.description: What the session may do through Dreamer, within the caller's own grant. Default: the terminal tools on every pane at the observe level.

harness.description: A harness from the agents settings; default agents.default.

model.description: Default agents.<harness>.model, else the harness's own default.

AgentSessionEvent.description: One normalised event, the same whatever the harness. Its shape follows the Agent Client Protocol: text and thinking arrive as deltas, a tool call as started, updated, and finished records with one id.

seq.description: Its place in the session's transcript, from 1.

AgentSessionEvents.description: The reply to agent.sessions.events, and the payload of each `agent.sessions.events` notification.

more.description: Without follow: more events follow the last one; ask again after it.

after.description: Events after this sequence number; default from the start of the transcript.

follow.description: Keep streaming: the reply carries no events, and `agent.sessions.events` notifications follow, the stored ones first. End it with terminal.unsubscribe.

for_pane.description: Read for the app in this app pane, as a desktop drawing a `transcript` bound to the session: the app's grant must allow agent.sessions.events and the session must be one the app may see, as well as the caller's.

limit.description: Without follow, the most events in the reply; default 1000, at most 10000.

text.description: The prompt. Sent while a turn runs, it waits for that turn to end.

AgentSessionStatus.description: The session changed state: the harness started, resumed, or ended, or the session closed.

output.description: Its output as text: the latest partial output, or the final one.

AgentUsage.description: Tokens of the latest model response, as the harness reports them.

cost_micro_usd.description: What the harness says it cost, in millionths of a US dollar.

AppCall.description: A call a web page of the app in pane makes through its bridge (window.dreamer.call), passed on by the desktop drawing the page. The daemon runs it as that app: under the app's grant, as the app's own connection would.

pane.description: The app pane whose page calls.

params.description: The method's parameters as JSON, as the API takes them; empty for none.

AppCapture.description: Ask the user's desktop for an image of an app pane as the desktop draws it natively (dream app preview --png).

path.description: Absolute path of the PNG file the desktop writes; replaced when it exists.

seq.description: Wait until the desktop has drawn at least this version of the pane's view tree; 0 takes what it shows.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the desktop's answer; default 10000, at most 60000.

error.description: Why this desktop wrote no image (for example, it does not show the pane); absent when it wrote one.

result.description: For a request with a method, its result as the API's JSON.

AppCaptureRequest.description: A capture for a desktop to make, answered with apps.capture_done.

id.description: 0 when no request came within the wait.

method.description: A web.* method (web.read, web.screenshot, web.click, web.type) to run on the pane's page instead of taking an image; empty for apps.capture.

params.description: That method's parameters, as the API's JSON.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for a request; default 20000, at most 60000. Answered with id 0 when none came.

key.description: A key by the app model's names: a character, Enter, Esc, Tab, Up, Ctrl-c, F2, ... Empty when the input is one of the fields below; exactly one is given.

node.description: In a view tree (manifest version 2), the node a click or wheel steps are for, by key; the host focuses it first. Without it they go to the focused node. Only with select or scroll.

scroll.description: Wheel steps: positive moves a table's or list's selection down, negative up.

select.description: A click: select this row of a table or list, or focus this form field, by index.

text.description: Text for the view's focused input (a text or number field, a prompt) as one edit: text committed by the platform's text input (IME) or pasted. Line breaks become spaces (a composer keeps them) and other control characters are dropped. A view with no focused input ignores it, so pasted text never runs a command.

live.description: The host is connected; when false, the tree is its last one.

patches.description: The changes from the caller's version, one JSON list of ops per version, in order.

revision.description: Grows with every new tree version and every change of `live`.

seq.description: The tree version the caller holds after applying this answer; 0 before the host's first tree.

tree.description: The whole tree as JSON, when the caller's version is unknown or too old for patches; else empty.

AppTreePublish.description: A version of an app host's view tree (docs/termapp.md, view trees): the whole tree, or the keyed changes from the version before.

patch.description: The changes from version seq - 1 as a JSON list of keyed ops; empty with a tree.

seq.description: This version; a patch's is one more than the version it changes.

tree.description: The whole tree as JSON (a frame: title, status, focus, root); empty with a patch.

after.description: Wait for a revision newer than this one; 0 answers at once.

seq.description: The tree version the caller holds; 0 for none. The answer brings it to the newest.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for a newer revision; default 20000, at most 60000.

live.description: The host is connected; when false, `view` is its last one.

revision.description: Grows with every new view and every change of `live`.

view.description: The latest model the host published, as JSON; empty before its first.
The app's model as JSON, as the app host draws it.

after.description: Wait for a revision newer than this one; 0 answers at once.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for a newer revision; default 20000, at most 60000. The current one is returned when it runs out.

Approval.description: An action waiting for the user: a connection at the elsewhere level acting on panes it did not create.

action.description: What it would do, in words.

closing.description: It closes panes or ends a program; `pane` approval does not cover it.

expires_unix_ms.description: Unanswered by then, it is denied.

panes.description: The panes it would act on that the requester did not create.

requester.description: Who asks: an app instance, or owner:N for a narrowed connection of the user's own.

snapshot.description: Engine snapshot; peers share the build family checked at handshake.

CollectCapture.description: What a row keeps besides its metadata.

after.description: Lines after a matched line to keep (at most 100).

before.description: Lines before a matched line to keep (at most 100).

fields.description: Fields from a line match: each value is a template where $1 or ${name} stands for a group.

json.description: The matched line is a JSON object: its top-level members become fields.

lines.description: Keep the pane's last N lines (at most 1000).

CollectFrom.description: The panes a collector covers: exactly one of these.

all.description: Every pane, including panes created later.

command.description: Panes whose current command (as tmux names it) matches this regular expression, while it does.

session.description: The panes of the session with this name.

value.description: Empty for rows without the field.

max_age_s.description: Rows older than this go. Default 7 days.

rows.description: Rows kept; the oldest go first. Default 5000, at most 100000.

after.description: Only rows after this row id: the first `limit` of them. Without it, the newest `limit`.

fields.description: Only rows with each of these fields at exactly this value.

group_by.description: Count rows by a field, or by pane, session, window, cwd, command, or trigger, instead of listing them.

delete.description: Also delete its definition and rows.

truncated.description: More rows matched than were returned.

CollectRow.description: One row of a collector's table.

after.description: Context lines after the matched line.

before.description: Context lines before the matched line, oldest first.

command.description: The command line the shell reported, else the pane's current command.

cwd.description: The pane's working directory: as the shell reports it (OSC 7), else its process's.

dropped.description: Rows this pane dropped (rate cap) since its previous recorded row.

exit_status.description: command_end: the status the shell reported.

id.description: Increases by one per row of the collector, across daemon restarts.

lines.description: The screen or the last lines, when capture asks for them.

trigger.description: line, command_end, idle, bell, exit, or interval.

CollectWhen.description: What makes a row: exactly one of these.

command_end.description: A command finished, as the shell reports it through shell integration (OSC 133).

every_s.description: Every this many seconds (at least 1); captures the screen unless capture says lines.

exit.description: The pane's process ended: the pane closed, died, or was respawned.

idle_ms.description: The pane wrote nothing for this long after writing something (at least 100).

line.description: A committed line matches this regular expression.

per_second.description: Rows per second per pane; more are dropped and counted. Default 10, at most 1000.

preset.description: A shipped definition to start from (errors, test-failures, commands, urls, paths); each part given here replaces the preset's. The name defaults to the preset's.

collected.description: Rows recorded since it was created.

dropped.description: Rows not recorded since it was created: over per_second, or the writer fell behind.

DaemonEvent.description: One entry of the daemon's event log: metadata only, never terminal content.

host.description: The remote host the event is about, if any.

kind.description: tmux.topology, actions.outcome, hosts.state, or apps.registered (see docs/events.md).

pane.description: The pane the event is about, if any.

sequence.description: Increases by one per event within a daemon instance, from 1.

state.description: An action outcome or a host's link state.

subject.description: An action id or launch id.

clients.description: Connected API clients, including the caller.

desktops.description: Desktop processes connected now that answer apps.capture.

heap_in_use.description: Bytes the daemon's allocator has handed out and not had back, without the freed memory it keeps for reuse; absent where the platform cannot tell.

Decoration.description: A mark on one line of a pane: data for clients to draw, never part of the terminal stream.

cols.description: The pane's width when marked; a reflow invalidates it.

row.description: The line's row counted from the top of the pane's history.

text.description: The line, as it was when marked.

decorations.description: Still valid: same generation and width, and the line is still at its row.

Diagnostics.description: The daemon's performance diagnostics. Timings and counters cover the time since diagnostics were turned on or reset, and only while on; queue depths are read now, on or off. Nothing here holds terminal content.

attach_queue.description: Panes waiting for a turn to attach.

backlog_panes.description: Panes with output held because their owner's queue is full.

checkpoints.description: Subscriptions (views, taps, collectors) started from a checkpoint.

cold_dropped_bytes.description: Output of Cold panes, dropped before any VT work.

collecting_ms.description: Since diagnostics were turned on or last reset.

event_queue.description: Events from tmux waiting for the mirror router.

lagged_subscribers.description: Subscriptions ended because their queue was full: dropped subscriber events, each reported to its subscriber as lagged.

parsed_bytes.description: Output bytes parsed by canonical mirrors.

parser_bytes_per_second.description: parsed_bytes over the time spent in the parse stage: the canonical parser's throughput while it works.

reattaches.description: Mirrors rebuilt from a fresh capture because a pane's output outran them.

records.description: Records (output chunks and resizes) applied by canonical mirrors.

replays.description: Subscriptions started by replaying the journal.

stages.description: The daemon's stages, in path order.

subscriber_queue_max.description: Records waiting in the fullest subscriber queue.

tmux_bytes.description: Bytes read from tmux's control output.

transferred_bytes.description: Terminal record bytes sent to subscribed clients, replays included.

worker_queues.description: Output messages waiting for each VT owner.

DiagnosticsSettings.description: Turn the daemon's performance diagnostics on or off. They are off by default, and cost nothing while off.

reset.description: Also start every timing and counter again from zero.

DrawerRequest.description: Which session's drawer, and where to show it. With none of session, window, or pane given the request is refused.

pane.description: The pane asking (a shell's TMUX_PANE): names the window and session when they are absent. The drawer pane itself names its own session.

session.description: The tmux session whose drawer this is.

window.description: The window to show it in; names the session when `session` is absent. Default: the session's active window.

command.description: The program and arguments it was started with; empty unless this call started it.

focused.description: The active pane of its window, and that window the session's active one.

from_pane.description: The pane that had focus before the drawer was last shown or focused, while it exists: where hiding returns focus, and the pane the harness's context commands read.

harness.description: The harness the pane was started with.

pane.description: The drawer's pane; absent while the session has none.

problem.description: Why the harness could not start; the pane says the same.

shown.description: In a window of the session (not the holding session).

window.description: The window the pane is in, the holding session's while hidden.

zoomed.description: Shown zoomed, because the window was too small to dock it.

EndpointStatus.description: One tmux server the daemon manages.

detail.description: Why the link is not live.

socket.description: tmux -L name or -S path, as configured.

EventBatch.description: Pushed as `events.batch`: a gap, if any, comes before the events.

cursor.description: Resume after this sequence to continue where this batch ends.

EventGap.description: Events in first..=last were not delivered; re-read state that depends on them.

after.description: Resume after this sequence; without it, only new events follow.

instance.description: The daemon instance the cursor came from (EventSubscription.instance).

kinds.description: Kinds or kind prefixes (`actions` matches `actions.outcome`); empty means every kind.

panes.description: Only events about these panes; empty means every event.

quota.description: How many events this subscriber may fall behind before it skips ahead with a gap; default 1024.

instance.description: This daemon instance; cursors are valid only within it.

oldest.description: The oldest sequence the log still keeps.

config_error.description: Why extensions.yaml could not be read; nothing was started from it.

failures.description: Consecutive failures; reset after a minute of running.

restarts.description: Times it was started again since the daemon started.

version.description: What it said in its extension.hello answer.

FilterInput.description: A typed trigger: fixed text typed into a pane. Matched text is never typed.

badge.description: The badge text for decorate: badge.

breaker.description: Triggers (topic, recipient, input) allowed in any 10 s; one more trips the filter. Default 50.

decorate.description: Mark each matched line on its pane (drawn by clients).

event.description: Record each match as a filters.matched event (scripts receive them with on_event).

grant.description: What the filter may do: taps.subscribe for its panes, plus what its outputs need.

input.description: Type this into a pane on each match.

name.description: Unique; its sender identity is filter:<name>.

pattern.description: As in terminal.query: a regular expression, or plain text with `literal`.

per_second.description: Matches acted on per second; more are counted as dropped. Default 20.

recipient.description: Send each matched line to this instance.

topic.description: Publish each matched line here (the derived stream).

reason.description: Why it is paused or tripped.

skipped_own.description: Lines skipped because they echo this filter's own input.

FocusInput.description: Sent to the application only if it asked for focus reports.

ForwardAck.description: Credit for a stream's incoming data, in bytes, given as the receiver passes data on.

ForwardData.description: Bytes of a forward stream, in order, in either direction.

eof.description: Nothing more follows in this direction (after data, if any).

error.description: Why the stream ended, when it failed.

ForwardOpen.description: A new stream to a port on this daemon's own loopback, for the coordinator's connection (forward.open). Its data arrives as `forward.data` bulk records, only as far as the caller's credit (forward.ack) allows.

stream.description: Unique within the daemon; belongs to the connection that opened it.

Grant.description: What a connection may do. The user's own clients hold the owner grant (everything). A narrow grant lists its methods (exact names, or `service.*`), the panes it may read, follow, or type into, and an optional expiry. Checked by the daemon before every request; data can never widen it.

level.description: How far the grant acts on panes; unspecified leaves it to the methods and panes alone.

owner.description: Everything is allowed (the user's own clients).

panes.description: Panes in scope; requests naming another pane are refused.

HostCall.description: One typed call forwarded to a connected host's daemon: `payload` is the method's parameters as Protobuf, exactly as in a local call. Methods that stream (subscriptions and watches) are refused.

HostConnect.description: Connect the local daemon (the coordinator) to the daemon on another host through system ssh, running `dream bridge --stdio` there. SSH configuration, keys, and host verification stay the user's.

auto_reconnect.description: Retry a dropped connection by itself; default: the profile's policy, or off for a host given here.

destination.description: SSH destination: host alias, user@host, or ssh:// URI.

dream.description: Remote dream executable; default `dream` on the remote PATH. A leading ~/ is the remote home.

name.description: A local label for this host; unique among hosts.

tmux.description: Remote tmux executable, for a remote daemon that has to be started.

HostFailure.description: Why the last attempt failed, and so whether retrying can help.

HostForward.description: A TCP port on a connected host's own loopback, to reach from this machine through the host's SSH connection (hosts.forward). Nothing on the host listens for it, and nothing is exposed on the network.

port.description: The port on the host's loopback (127.0.0.1, else ::1).

HostForwarded.description: A forward held by the calling connection until hosts.unforward or until the connection closes. Holds of one host port share one listener, closed when the last hold goes.

local_port.description: The port on this machine's 127.0.0.1 that reaches the host's port.

HostList.description: Every profile in hosts.yaml and every other host connected since the daemon started.

profiles_error.description: hosts.yaml exists but is invalid: the error, with its location.

HostReply.description: The remote daemon's result for a HostCall, as Protobuf.

attempts.description: Failed attempts since the last live connection.

detail.description: Why the host is not live: the reason and SSH's last diagnostic lines.

last_contact_unix_ms.description: Last successful exchange with the remote daemon.

next_retry_unix_ms.description: When the next automatic attempt starts, if one is scheduled.

remote.description: The remote daemon's protocol and build, once live.

remote_instance.description: Changes when the remote daemon restarts.

HostSubscribe.description: Follow a pane on a connected host through this daemon: the reply and the `terminal.*` events are those of terminal.subscribe, with this connection's own subscription id. When SSH drops and the host comes back, the subscription resumes from the host's journal by itself; it ends with host_lost or host_restarted when it cannot.

bytes.description: Encoded bytes delivered to the pane.

plan_id.description: The id of the reviewed plan; a different plan now is refused.

InstallPlan.description: What hosts.install would do, for review: found by probing the host through SSH. Installing requires this plan's id, so nothing different from what was reviewed can be installed.

installed.description: The installed server's VERSION first line, if any.

steps.description: Each change, in order, in plain words.

target.description: The matching Rust target, such as x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.

version.description: The version that would be installed (this daemon's own).

artifacts.description: Directory of server archives on this machine; default DREAMER_SERVER_ARTIFACTS, else share/dreamer/server beside this daemon.

check.description: What the installed dream --version printed on the host.

remote_dream.description: The installed dream, as run on the host.

artifacts.description: The directory the job was given as DREAMER_JOB_ARTIFACTS.

pane.description: Its tmux pane: read its output with terminal.read while the pane remains.

argv.description: The exact program and arguments; no shell.

env.description: Added to the job's environment; names are [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*.

name.description: The tmux window name; default the program's name.

session.description: The session for its window; default the first session.

KeyInput.description: A key press, encoded by the daemon with the pane's current keyboard modes.

held.description: An auto-repeat of a key held down.

key.description: W3C KeyboardEvent.code name: KeyA, Digit1, ArrowUp, Enter, F5, ...

text.description: The text the key produced on the client keyboard layout.

KeyOptions.description: tmux's global key and copy-mode options, as tmux reports them. Read only: Dreamer never changes them.

mode_style.description: As tmux reports it, for example bg=yellow,fg=black.

prefix.description: A tmux key name such as C-b, or None.

prefix2.description: A tmux key name, or None.

endpoint.description: Endpoint name; the default endpoint when absent.

LaunchApp.description: Start a program in a new tmux window as a registered app. The daemon writes a single-use ticket to an owner-only file and gives the program only that file's path (DREAMER_LAUNCH_TICKET) and the launch id (DREAMER_LAUNCH_ID). The program registers with them for `grant`.

argv.description: Exact program and arguments; never a shell string.

grant.description: What the app may do; with no panes and not all_panes, its own pane.

name.description: The window name; default the app id.

split.description: Open the app in a pane split from this one, side by side, instead of a new window of `session`.

ttl_ms.description: How long the ticket is valid; default 60000.

generation.description: Increases with every lease on the pane; a revoked generation never comes back.

LeaseAcquire.description: Ask to type into a pane as automation. One connection holds a pane's lease at a time; it expires unless used, and a person typing into the pane revokes it.

ttl_ms.description: Idle time before the lease expires: default 30000, at most 600000. Each use starts it again.

MemoryContext.description: Who is asking, for the project and session scopes.

cwd.description: The caller's working directory; the project is the nearest directory above it holding .dreamer/memory, else its git root, else the directory itself.

session.description: The agent session id, for the session scope.

id.description: Stable while the memory exists; for the files provider, the scope and the file's name without .md (user/prefers-tabs).

links.description: Paths, URLs, or other memories' ids.

path.description: The file that holds it, for a provider that keeps files.

score.description: memory.recall: how well it matched; higher is better.

provider.description: The provider in force (files, sqlite, or kosmonaut).

MemoryKind.description: What a memory is about; the same kinds as Claude Code's memory.

scope.description: Unspecified: every scope the context reaches.

MemoryProblem.description: A memory file that could not be read; it is left as it is and skipped.

query.description: Words to look for; empty returns the newest.

scope.description: Unspecified: every scope the context reaches.

context.description: Needed for an id in the project or session scope.

title.description: Default: the text's first line, shortened.

MemoryScope.description: Where a memory applies. Unspecified in a query means every scope the caller's context reaches.

MemoryTransfer.description: Which memories memory.import and memory.export copy.

scope.description: Unspecified: every scope the context reaches.

problems.description: Memory files that could not be read; they are left out.

MemoryUpdate.description: Change a memory; what is not given stays.

missed.description: Messages dropped for this subscription since the previous delivery, because it was full.

cause.description: The message this one answers or was caused by.

claimed_sender.description: What the sender said about itself: a claim, never authority.

id.description: Assigned by the daemon; increases per message.

origin.description: The first message of this causal chain (its own id when it starts one).

recipient.description: The instance a direct message, request, or reply is for.

request.description: A request: answer it with messages.reply.

schema.description: The payload's schema version, chosen by the sender.

MessagePublish.description: A topic message or a direct message: give exactly one of topic and recipient.

sender.description: A claimed sender; recipients see it as claimed_sender, next to the stamped one.

topic.description: Not dreamer.*, human.*, policy.*, or approval.*: those are the daemon's.

MessageSender.description: Who sent a message, stamped by the daemon from the connection; never taken from the sender.

instance.description: A registered app's instance, or owner:<n> for one of the user's own clients.

topics.description: Exact topics, service.* prefixes, or *. Direct messages and requests to this connection arrive regardless.

instance.description: This connection's identity as a recipient.

cwd.description: Latest working directory the program reported (OSC 7).

journal_first_sequence.description: Oldest retained journal record; sequence + 1 when none is retained.

reattaches.description: Times the mirror was rebuilt from a fresh capture because the pane's output outran it.

MouseInput.description: A mouse event at a cell of the pane's canonical grid, encoded with the application's mouse tracking mode and format. Nothing is sent when the application does not track this kind of event. Wheel steps are presses of wheel_up or wheel_down, one per step.

buttons_held.description: A button is down (for drag reporting).

MovePane.description: Move a pane, with its process, into another window: an existing one (`window`), or a new window of its own named `new_window` in the pane's session. Exactly one of the two. The pane keeps its id.

NewSession.description: A new detached session with one window; it runs the default shell unless argv is given. tmux names it when `name` is absent. The record's `new_pane` is its first pane.

argv.description: Exact program and arguments; never a shell string.

NewWindow.description: A window at the end of a session; it runs the default shell unless argv is given.

argv.description: Exact program and arguments; never a shell string.

app.description: The registered app whose host is this pane's program, if any: desktops draw its view (apps.view) in the pane's rectangle instead of the terminal.

drawer_of.description: This pane is the harness drawer of that tmux session (drawer.toggle).

generation.description: Process generation; changes when the pane is respawned.

mode.description: A tmux-drawn mode the pane is in (copy-mode, tree-mode, ...). Its screen is tmux's, not the program's, and Dreamer does not draw it.

web.description: This pane is a placeholder for a web page at this URL (web.open): desktops that can draw web pages show the page in the pane's rectangle instead of the terminal; other clients see the placeholder's text.

web_scroll_x.description: A web pane's scroll position in CSS pixels as the desktop drawing it last reported it (web.state), kept in the placeholder for the page to open there again; 0 before a report.

live.description: The host is connected. When false, apps.view keeps its last view, to be shown as stale.

PasteInput.description: Bracketed exactly once when the application enabled bracketed paste. A paste larger than one request is sent in parts with the same id and `more` set on all but the last; the daemon encodes the whole paste once (at most 64 MiB).

endpoint.description: Endpoint name; the default endpoint when absent.

key.description: One tmux key name (c, C-o, M-Up, PPage), typed after the prefix.

pane.description: The pane the key is typed on.

mode_cancelled.description: A mode the binding opened on the pane (copy-mode, tree-mode, ...), which was cancelled: tmux draws modes only for ordinary clients.

panes.description: Only processes in these panes; empty means every process of the user (needs all_panes).

provider.description: Only runs of this provider: claude or codex.
